description: Get a daily calendar summary in Slack: the Google Calendar app on paid Slack plans, an automation, or an AI agent that sends tomorrow’s meetings.
h1: How to get a daily calendar summary in Slack
answer: On a paid Slack plan, turn on the Google Calendar app's daily schedule in its Home tab, under Settings.
On free Slack, or for tomorrow's meetings the evening before, use an automation or an AI agent.

root.q: When do you plan your day?

then.q: Are you on a paid Slack plan?

then.why: Its daily schedule sends today's events each morning, at a time you pick in the app's settings. The least work of any option.
Calendar, then Slack, at a fixed time: a plain list of today's meetings, and free Slack works.

then.q: Do you want a note on what to prepare?

then.why: The built-in app only sends today's schedule. An automation can send tomorrow's list at 18:00.
It reads tomorrow's meetings and adds judgement: clashes, gaps, and what is worth preparing.

method.h2: How to get a daily calendar summary in Slack

steps.title: Pick the calendar and the window
steps.body: Your primary calendar, or a shared team one. Today from 00:00 to 23:59, or tomorrow, in your timezone.

steps.title: Pick the time
steps.body: 18:00 for tomorrow lets you prepare tonight; 8:00 for today is a morning check. Never midnight, when nobody reads it.

steps.title: Send it to yourself, not a channel
steps.body: A direct message keeps private event titles private. Post to a channel only from a shared team calendar.

note.text: "Doctor" or "Interview: Jane Doe" posted to a team channel cannot be taken back once people have read it.

steps.title: Decide what each line shows
steps.body: Time, title, who, and where (room or video link). Skip descriptions; they are long and often private.

steps.title: Test the edge cases
steps.body: All-day events, declined invites, a recurring event moved this once, and travel across timezones. Test a day with each.

captain.line: Captain builds an AI agent with Google Calendar and Slack that sends you tomorrow's meetings each evening, with any clash and anything worth preparing.

wrong.title: No schedule on free Slack
wrong.body: The Google Calendar app's daily schedule needs a paid plan. Use an automation or an AI agent instead.

wrong.title: Times off by an hour
wrong.body: The tool used UTC or the wrong timezone. Set the window and the send time in your timezone.

wrong.title: Declined meetings still listed
wrong.body: Events you said no to clutter the list. Filter out declined events, and mark tentative ones.

wrong.title: Status sync fights you
wrong.body: Slack's calendar status follows your primary calendar only and never overrides a status you set yourself. Expect gaps there.

faqs.q: Can Slack show my daily schedule?
faqs.a: Yes, on paid plans, through the Google Calendar for Slack app's daily schedule notification. Turn it on in the app's Home tab, under Settings.

faqs.q: Can I get tomorrow's meetings the night before?
faqs.a: Not from the built-in app, which sends today's schedule. An automation or AI agent on an evening schedule can.

faqs.q: Does it work with Outlook calendars?
faqs.a: Slack has an Outlook Calendar app too, and automation tools connect to Outlook. The steps above are the same.

faqs.q: Should the summary go to a channel or a direct message?
faqs.a: A direct message for your own calendar, so private titles stay private. A channel only for a shared team calendar, with titles everyone may see.

faqs.q: What should each line of the summary show?
faqs.a: Time, title, who, and where: a room or a video link. Skip descriptions; they are long and often private.

faqs.q: Why are my meeting times an hour off?
faqs.a: The tool is reading the calendar in a different timezone, or a daylight saving change happened. Set the timezone in the tool and test a day when you travel.
